title.en: Volume 470 Biographies 257: Zhi Rui, With: Liu Congde, Chun Xun, Liang Bi, Zong Shizaimu, Wan Xuan With: De Pei, Tong Yuan, Wen Rui With: Cheng Yan, Ke Meng E, Heng Ling With: De Pei, Pu Shou, Xie Baosheng, Yao Aiyun, Huang Zhonghao, Yang Rang Li Cong Zi Xu : Chen Qi
title.raw: 卷470 列傳二百五十七 志锐 附：刘从德 春勋 良弼 宗室载穆 万选附：德霈 同源 文瑞附：承燕 克蒙额 恒龄附：德霈 樸寿 谢宝胜 姚霭雲 黄忠浩 杨让梨从子壻：陈萁

sentences.zh: 列傳二百五十七

translations.literal: Biographies, number 257.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 257

sentences.zh: 志銳劉從德春勳良弼宗室載穆萬選德霈同源

translations.literal: Zhi Rui, Liu Congde, Chun Xun, Liang Bi, Zongshi Zaimu, Wan Xuan, De Pei, Tong Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Rui; with Liu Congde, Chun Xun, Liang Bi, Zongshi Zaimu, Wan Xuan; with De Pei and Tong Yuan

sentences.zh: 文瑞承燕克蒙額恆齡德霈等樸壽謝寶勝姚靄雲

translations.literal: Wen Rui, Cheng Yan, Ke Meng'e, Heng Ling, De Pei, and others; Pu Shou, Xie Baosheng, Yao Aiyun.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Rui; with Cheng Yan, Ke Meng'e, and Heng Ling; with De Pei, Pu Shou, Xie Baosheng, and Yao Aiyun

sentences.zh: 黃忠浩楊讓梨等志銳，字公穎，他塔拉氏，世居扎庫木，隸滿洲正紅旗，陝甘總督裕泰孫。

translations.literal: Huang Zhonghao, Yang Rangli, and others. Zhi Rui, styled Gongying, was of the Tatara clan, long resident at Zhakumu, registered in the Manchu Plain Red Banner, and was grandson of Yu Tai, Governor-General of Shaanxi and Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zhonghao, Yang Rangli, and the others are treated below. Zhi Rui, styled Gongying, belonged to the Tatara clan and had lived for generations at Zhakumu. He was enrolled in the Manchu Plain Red Banner and was a grandson of Yu Tai, governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu.

sentences.zh: 父長敬，四川綏定府知府。

translations.literal: His father Chang Jing was prefect of Suiding Prefecture in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Chang Jing, served as prefect of Suiding in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 志銳幼穎異，光緒六年成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: Zhi Rui was precocious in youth. In the sixth year of Guangxu he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Zhi Rui showed unusual brilliance. In 1880 he passed the metropolitan examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 與黃體芳、盛昱輩相勵以風節，數上書言事。

translations.literal: He and Huang Tifang, Sheng Yu, and their circle urged one another in moral integrity, and he repeatedly submitted memorials on public affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He and such men as Huang Tifang and Sheng Yu spurred one another to uphold integrity, and he sent up memorial after memorial on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 累遷詹事，擢禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and then to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and was then promoted to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 中東事起，上疏畫戰守策累萬言。

translations.literal: When the Sino-Japanese conflict arose, he submitted a memorial setting forth war and defense plans in tens of thousands of words.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out with Japan, he submitted a memorial of many thousand words outlining strategies for offense and defense.

sentences.zh: 慮陪都警，自請募勇設防，稱旨，命赴熱河練兵。

translations.literal: Fearing an alarm at the secondary capital, he volunteered to raise troops and set up defenses. The throne approved and ordered him to Rehe to drill troops.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed at the prospect of danger to the secondary capital, he asked to raise volunteers and organize defenses. The court approved and sent him to Rehe to train troops.

sentences.zh: 未踰月，以其妹瑾、珍兩妃貶貴人，降授烏里雅蘇台參贊大臣，釋兵柄。

translations.literal: Within a month, because his younger sisters the Consorts Jin and Zhen were demoted to noble ladies, he was reduced and appointed Assistant Minister at Uliastai, and his military authority was removed.
translations.idiomatic: Before a month had passed, his younger sisters the consorts Jin and Zhen were demoted to noble ladies. He was stripped of his command and demoted to assistant minister at Uliastai.

sentences.zh: 遂迂道出張家口，策馬逾天山西絕幕。

translations.literal: He then took a circuitous route out through Zhangjiakou and rode his horse across the Tianshan into the far western desert.
translations.idiomatic: He left by a roundabout route through Zhangjiakou and rode on horseback across the Tianshan into the desolate western frontier.

sentences.zh: 所迳台站，輒週諮山川、風俗、宗教，箸詩記事。

translations.literal: At every courier station along the way he would inquire broadly about mountains and rivers, customs, and religion, and compose poetry to record what he saw.
translations.idiomatic: At each relay station along the route he questioned people about the land, local customs, and religion, and wrote poems to record his journey.

sentences.zh: 居數年，將軍長庚令赴邊外釐​​中俄積案，凡六閱月，結千餘起。

translations.literal: After several years, the general Chang Geng ordered him to go beyond the border to settle accumulated Sino-Russian cases. In six months he closed more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: After several years General Chang Geng sent him beyond the frontier to clear long-standing Sino-Russian disputes. In six months he settled more than a thousand cases.

sentences.zh: 前後五上疏籌西北防務，發強鄰狡謀，中當軸忌，左遷索倫領隊大臣。

translations.literal: Before and after he submitted five memorials planning northwestern defenses, exposing the crafty designs of a powerful neighbor. This offended those in power, and he was demoted to Solon Brigade Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He sent up five memorials in all on northwestern defense, laying bare the schemes of an aggressive neighbor. The men at the center of power took offense, and he was demoted to Solon brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 領隊例不得專摺奏事，居則鉤稽地形戹塞，出則徼循鄂博、卡倫，冀得當以報。

translations.literal: By regulation a brigade commander might not submit memorials on his own authority. When at home he investigated terrain and strategic passes; when abroad he patrolled obos and frontier posts, hoping for an opportunity to repay the court.
translations.idiomatic: Brigade commanders were not allowed to submit memorials on their own. At his post he studied the terrain and strategic choke points; in the field he patrolled border markers and frontier stations, hoping for a chance to serve the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 又數年，改授寧夏副都統，疏請發帑二十萬濬城外故渠，獲沃壤數千頃。

translations.literal: After several more years he was transferred to vice commander at Ningxia. He memorialized requesting two hundred thousand taels from the treasury to dredge the old canal outside the city and recovered several thousand qing of fertile land.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was appointed vice commander at Ningxia. He asked the court for two hundred thousand taels to dredge an old canal outside the walls and reclaimed several thousand qing of rich farmland.

sentences.zh: 頻上疏，多言人所不敢言。

translations.literal: He submitted memorials frequently, often saying what others dared not say.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again and again, often speaking plainly where others would not dare.

sentences.zh: 宣統二年，遷杭州將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuantong he was transferred to General at Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1910 he was transferred to the post of general at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，調伊犁將軍，加尚書銜。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to General at Yili, with the nominal rank of minister.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was moved to general at Yili and given the nominal rank of a ministry president.

sentences.zh: 入覲，條上弭邊患、禦外侮機宜甚悉；

translations.literal: On entering audience he itemized in detail measures to quell border troubles and repel foreign aggression;
translations.idiomatic: On audience with the throne he laid out in detail how to ease border troubles and resist foreign aggression;

sentences.zh: 又力陳新政多糜費，請省罷，壹意練兵救危局。

translations.literal: he also urged forcefully that the new policies wasted much money and asked that they be cut back, devoting effort solely to drilling troops to save the desperate situation.
translations.idiomatic: and he argued forcefully that the new reforms wasted money, urging that they be pared back so the court could concentrate on training troops to rescue the realm.

sentences.zh: 並請邊地練兵費百萬，部議止予二十萬。

translations.literal: He also requested a million taels for frontier troop training; the ministry deliberated and granted only two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked for a million taels to train troops on the frontier, but the ministries approved only two hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 抵新疆，聞武昌變，或勸少留，不可。

translations.literal: On reaching Xinjiang he heard of the Wuchang uprising. Some urged him to delay briefly; he would not.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Xinjiang he heard of the uprising at Wuchang. Some advised him to wait awhile; he refused.

sentences.zh: 踰月，到官，日討軍士而申儆之。

translations.literal: After more than a month he took office and daily drilled the soldiers, admonishing them sternly.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he assumed his post and drilled the troops every day, warning them sharply of their duty.

sentences.zh: 已，蘭州軍譁變，寧夏繼之。

translations.literal: Soon after, the troops at Lanzhou mutinied, and Ningxia followed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the garrison at Lanzhou mutinied, and Ningxia did the same.

sentences.zh: 伊犁協統楊纘緒以兵叛，夜據南北軍器庫，攻將軍署。

translations.literal: Yang Zuanxu, assistant commander at Yili, rebelled with troops. By night he seized the northern and southern arsenals and attacked the general's yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zuanxu, the assistant commander at Yili, rose in revolt. That night his men seized the northern and southern arsenals and assaulted the general's residence.

sentences.zh: 群議舉志銳為都督，峻拒之；

translations.literal: The crowd proposed making Zhi Rui military governor; he sternly refused;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels proposed making Zhi Rui military governor; he flatly refused;

sentences.zh: 迫詣商會，亦弗從，起發槍擊之，遂遇害。

translations.literal: when forced to go to the chamber of commerce he still would not comply. He rose and fired at them and was thereupon killed.
translations.idiomatic: when they forced him to the chamber of commerce he still would not yield. He rose and opened fire on them, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 其僕呂順奔走營棺斂，撫屍號慟，亦為叛軍所戕。

translations.literal: His servant Lü Shun ran about arranging a coffin and burial, embraced the corpse and wailed, and was also slain by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: His servant Lü Shun rushed about to secure a coffin, embraced the body and wept aloud, and was killed by the rebels as well.

sentences.zh: 又武巡捕官劉從德四川人、教練官春勳京旗人，並及於難。

translations.literal: Also the armed patrol officer Liu Congde, a native of Sichuan, and the drill officer Chun Xun, a man of the Metropolitan Banners, perished in the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The armed patrol officer Liu Congde of Sichuan and the drill officer Chun Xun of the Metropolitan Banners also died in the turmoil.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈志銳太子少保，諡文貞。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Zhi Rui was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Zhi Rui was posthumously made junior guardian of the heir apparent and given the posthumous name Wenzhen, "Loyal and Upright."

sentences.zh: 志銳夙負奇氣，守邊庭逾十稔，自號為窮塞主。

translations.literal: Zhi Rui had long borne an extraordinary spirit. He guarded the frontier for more than ten years and styled himself Master of the Desolate Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Rui had always been a man of fierce spirit. He held the frontier for more than ten years and called himself Master of the Desolate Pass.

sentences.zh: 工詩詞。

translations.literal: He was skilled in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He was accomplished in poetry.

sentences.zh: 熟察邊情，懼禍至無日。

translations.literal: He knew the border situation well and feared disaster might come any day.
translations.idiomatic: He knew the frontier situation intimately and feared catastrophe was only a matter of time.

sentences.zh: 其赴伊犁也，以手書遍告戚友，言「以身許國，不作生入玉門想」。

translations.literal: When he set out for Yili he wrote by hand to all his kin and friends, saying, "I devote my body to the state and do not expect to pass alive through the Jade Gate."
translations.idiomatic: When he left for Yili he wrote by hand to relatives and friends everywhere, saying, "I give my life to the country and do not expect to return alive through the Jade Gate."

sentences.zh: 其致命遂志，蓋已定於拜疏出國門日雲。

translations.literal: His resolve to die for his purpose was surely fixed from the day he submitted his memorial and passed out the capital gate.
translations.idiomatic: His determination to die for his convictions had been settled, it seems, from the day he submitted his memorial and left the capital.

sentences.zh: 良弼，字賚臣，紅帶子，隸鑲黃旗，大學士伊里布孫。

translations.literal: Liang Bi, styled Baichen, was a girdled bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner and grandson of the Grand Secretary Yilibu.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Bi, styled Baichen, was a girdled bannerman enrolled in the Bordered Yellow Banner and a grandson of Grand Secretary Yilibu.

sentences.zh: 少孤，事母孝。

translations.literal: He lost his father young and served his mother with filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, he was devoted to his mother.

sentences.zh: 劬學，留學日本陸軍學校，畢業歸，入練兵處。

translations.literal: He studied diligently, went abroad to the Japanese Army School, returned after graduation, and entered the Army Training Office.
translations.idiomatic: He studied hard, trained at the Japanese Army School, returned after graduation, and joined the Army Training Office.

sentences.zh: 歷陸軍部軍學司監督副使，補司長。

translations.literal: He served as deputy director of the Military Studies Bureau in the Ministry of Army and was then made bureau chief.
translations.idiomatic: He served as deputy director of the military studies bureau in the army ministry and was later appointed bureau chief.

sentences.zh: 時新設禁衛軍，任第一協統領兼鑲白旗都統，遷軍諮府軍諮使。

translations.literal: When the new Imperial Guard was established he was made commander of the First Brigade and concurrently commander of the Bordered White Banner, then transferred to military adviser in the General Staff.
translations.idiomatic: When the new Imperial Guard was formed he commanded its first brigade and concurrently headed the Bordered White Banner, and was later made a military adviser on the general staff.

sentences.zh: 平日以知兵名，改軍制，練新軍，立軍學，良弼皆主其謀。

translations.literal: He was known in ordinary times for military expertise. Reform of the army system, training of new forces, and founding of military schools—all these plans Liang Bi chiefly directed.
translations.idiomatic: He was widely known as a military expert. Army reform, training of new forces, and founding military schools—all bore his stamp.

sentences.zh: 尤留意人才，自將帥以至軍士，莫不延納。

translations.literal: He paid special attention to talent, from generals down to common soldiers, welcoming all without exception.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially attentive to talent, recruiting officers and enlisted men alike.

sentences.zh: 思有所建樹，頗為時忌。

translations.literal: He wished to achieve something and was much resented by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: He hoped to accomplish great things, and many at court resented him for it.

sentences.zh: 武昌亂起，各省響應，朝論紛呶，王公貴人皆氣餒，莫知所為。

translations.literal: When disorder broke out at Wuchang and provinces responded in turn, court debate was clamorous. Princes, dukes, and nobles were all dispirited and knew not what to do.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion erupted at Wuchang and province after province followed, the court was in an uproar. Princes and nobles lost heart and had no idea what to do.

sentences.zh: 良弼獨與三數才傑朝夕規畫，外聯群帥，內安當國，思以立憲弭革命，圖救大局，上下皆恃以為重。

translations.literal: Liang Bi alone with a few outstanding men planned day and night, linking commanders abroad and steadying those in power at home, thinking to quell revolution by constitutionalism and save the overall situation. High and low all relied on him as a mainstay.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Bi alone, with a handful of able men, plotted day and night—rallying commanders in the provinces, steadying those who held power in the capital—hoping constitutional rule might halt the revolution and save the dynasty. Court and country alike looked to him.

sentences.zh: 時袁世凱來京，方議國體，人心不安甚矣。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Shikai came to the capital while the form of government was under debate, and popular anxiety was extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shikai had come to Beijing while the form of government was still in dispute, and public anxiety ran very high.

sentences.zh: 一日，良弼議事歸，及門，有人遽擲炸彈，三日而卒。

translations.literal: One day Liang Bi returned from a council. At the gate someone suddenly threw a bomb; he died three days later.
translations.idiomatic: One day, as Liang Bi returned from a meeting and reached his gate, an assassin hurled a bomb. He died three days later.

sentences.zh: 事聞，震悼，優恤如例。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported the court was shaken with grief and granted generous condolence according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne the court was shaken with grief and granted the usual generous posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 其後官紳請立祠於北京祀之。

translations.literal: Afterward officials and gentry asked to erect a shrine in Beijing to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: Later officials and local gentry petitioned to build a shrine in Beijing in his honor.

sentences.zh: 良弼剛果有骨氣，頗自負，雖參軍務，無可與謀，常以不得行其志為恨，日有憂色。

translations.literal: Liang Bi was firm and spirited, rather self-assured. Though he took part in military affairs, he had no one with whom to plan, and often grieved that he could not carry out his aims, his face daily clouded with worry.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Bi was resolute and proud. Though he took part in military affairs, he had no true partner in counsel and brooded that he could not put his plans into effect; worry showed on his face every day.

sentences.zh: 及遇刺，醫初謂可療，忽有進以酒者，遂死。

translations.literal: When he was attacked, physicians at first said he could be cured, but suddenly someone brought him wine and he died.
translations.idiomatic: After the attack physicians at first thought he might recover, but someone then gave him wine and he died.

sentences.zh: 死未旬日，而遜位詔下，時皆悼之。

translations.literal: Less than ten days after his death the abdication edict was issued, and all mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days of his death the abdication edict was promulgated, and contemporaries mourned him all the more.

sentences.zh: 宗室載穆，字敬修，隸滿洲鑲藍旗，恂勤郡王允禵五世孫。

translations.literal: Zongshi Zaimu, styled Jingxiu, was enrolled in the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner and was a fifth-generation descendant of Prince Xunqin Yunti.
translations.idiomatic: Zongshi Zaimu, styled Jingxiu, was enrolled in the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner and a fifth-generation descendant of Prince Xunqin Yunti.

sentences.zh: 祖綿翔，鎮國將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mianxiang held the rank of Defender of the State.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mianxiang held the rank of defender of the state.

sentences.zh: 父奕雲，一等侍衛，記名副都統。

translations.literal: His father Yiyun was a first-class bodyguard and recorded vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yiyun was a first-class imperial bodyguard with the recorded rank of vice commander.

sentences.zh: 載穆年二十，除三等侍衛，累遷頭等，兼辦事章京。

translations.literal: At twenty Zaimu was appointed third-class bodyguard, was promoted in succession to first class, and also served as a clerical secretary.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty Zaimu was appointed a third-class bodyguard, rose to first class, and also served as a clerical secretary.

sentences.zh: 以忼直忤上官意，數歲不遷。

translations.literal: Because of his upright and unyielding manner he offended his superiors and for several years received no promotion.
translations.idiomatic: His blunt integrity offended his superiors, and for years he received no promotion.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十六年，拳亂起，兩宮西幸，痛哭自盡者再，遇救獲免。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Guangxu the Boxer turmoil arose and the two palaces fled west. Twice he wept and tried to kill himself, but was rescued and spared.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900, when the Boxer rising broke out and the court fled west, he twice wept and tried to take his own life but was saved each time.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，授太原城守尉。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was appointed garrison commander of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1906 he was appointed garrison commander of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 明年，有詔遞裁駐防，分遣歸農，乃倡農桑，勸女工，興學校。

translations.literal: The next year an edict ordered successive reductions of garrison forces and dispatch of men back to farming. He then promoted agriculture and sericulture, encouraged women's weaving, and founded schools.
translations.idiomatic: The next year an edict called for successive cuts to the garrisons and the return of bannermen to farming. He promoted agriculture and sericulture, encouraged women's weaving, and opened schools.

sentences.zh: 比去晉，旗民男婦務耕作、嫺織紝者達二百人。

translations.literal: By the time he left Shanxi, banner men and women engaged in farming or skilled in weaving numbered two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he left Shanxi, two hundred banner men and women were working the fields or weaving skillfully.

sentences.zh: 省城門有八，舊閉其二。

translations.literal: The provincial capital had eight gates; two had long been closed.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial capital had eight gates, two of which had long been closed.

sentences.zh: 阜城門當汾水沖，河決土壅，不能通車馬，群議閉之。

translations.literal: The Fucheng Gate faced the Fen River flood line. When the river broke its banks earth piled up and neither carts nor horses could pass; the crowd debated closing it.
translations.idiomatic: The Fucheng Gate lay in the path of the Fen River. After a breach the silt piled up until neither carts nor horses could pass, and many argued the gate should be shut permanently.

sentences.zh: 載穆曰：「此汾西數十村入城孔道也，請於舊門南闢新門。」

translations.literal: Zaimu said: "This is the main route by which dozens of villages west of the Fen enter the city. I ask that a new gate be opened south of the old one."
translations.idiomatic: Zaimu said, "This is the main route by which dozens of villages west of the Fen enter the city. Open a new gate south of the old one instead."

sentences.zh: 民稱便。

translations.literal: The people praised the convenience.
translations.idiomatic: The people welcomed the change.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，將入覲，巡撫丁寶楨疏留之，報可。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he was to enter audience, Governor Ding Baozhen memorialized to retain him; the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended and he was due at court, Governor Ding Baozhen memorialized to keep him in post, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年，簡京口副都統。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuantong he was selected as vice commander at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1911 he was appointed vice commander at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 鄂難作，緣江戒嚴。

translations.literal: When trouble arose in Hubei, the Yangzi valley was placed under martial alert.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion broke out in Hubei, the Yangzi valley was placed under martial law.

sentences.zh: 載穆繕城郭，犒軍士，設練兵處，定營防城守章條，晝夜徼循，旗、漢民雜居者皆安堵。

translations.literal: Zaimu repaired walls and moats, rewarded the troops, established a training office, set regulations for camp defense and city garrison, and patrolled day and night. Banner and Han residents living together were all settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zaimu repaired the walls, rewarded the troops, set up a training office, and drew up rules for camp defense and city garrison, patrolling day and night until banner and Han residents alike lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 已而新軍徙頓鐵道旁，運槍械者繦屬。

translations.literal: Soon the new army shifted camp beside the railway, and those transporting arms and munitions came in an unbroken stream.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the new army encamped beside the railway, and convoys of arms and ammunition passed without cease.

sentences.zh: 載穆知有異，遣使如江寧告急，弗應。

translations.literal: Zaimu knew something was amiss and sent envoys to Jiangning to plead for aid; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Zaimu sensed trouble and sent messengers to Jiangning to plead for help, but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 江蘇巡撫程德全號獨立，傳檄鎮江，防營乃潛通蘇軍，全城益怖懼。

translations.literal: Jiangsu Governor Cheng Dequan declared independence and sent a proclamation to Zhenjiang. The defense garrison then secretly communicated with Jiangsu forces, and fear throughout the city grew.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangsu governor Cheng Dequan declared independence and sent a proclamation to Zhenjiang. The defense garrison secretly contacted Jiangsu troops, and terror spread through the city.

sentences.zh: 於是官紳集議，定滿、漢聯合策，約毋戰，且要旗營繳軍械。

translations.literal: Thereupon officials and gentry met and settled on a Manchu-Han joint policy, agreeing not to fight and demanding that the banner camp surrender its arms.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and gentry then met and agreed on a joint Manchu-Han policy not to fight, demanding that the banner garrison surrender its weapons.

sentences.zh: 載穆知事不可為，罷會大慟，語左右曰：「吾上負朝廷，所欠止一死耳！」

translations.literal: Zaimu knew the situation could not be saved. When the meeting ended he wept greatly and said to those beside him, "I have failed the court above; all I owe now is death!"
translations.idiomatic: Zaimu saw that nothing could be done. When the meeting ended he broke down in tears and told his attendants, "I have failed the dynasty; all that remains for me is to die."

sentences.zh: 左右環跽，請系眾心，維危局。

translations.literal: His attendants knelt all around him, begging him to steady popular sentiment and preserve the desperate situation.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants knelt around him and begged him to steady the people and hold the crisis together.

sentences.zh: 翼日，鎮紳楊邦彥詣軍門趣繳械，不許。

translations.literal: The next day the local gentleman Yang Bangyan came to the military gate to urge surrender of arms; permission was refused.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the local gentleman Yang Bangyan came to headquarters to press for the surrender of arms; Zaimu refused.

sentences.zh: 會新軍入據漢城，旗營大譁，乃進旗眾而語之曰：「駐防兵單糧儲竭，吾戰死甘如飴。

translations.literal: Just then the new army entered and occupied the Han city quarter; the banner camp was in an uproar. He went before the banner masses and said, "The garrison is few, provisions are exhausted; I would gladly die in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The new army then seized the Han quarter of the city and the banner camp erupted. Zaimu went before the banner people and said, "Our garrison is small and our stores are gone. I would gladly die fighting.

sentences.zh: 顧糜吾民肝腦膏鋒刃，吾奚忍？

translations.literal: Yet to waste our people's lives and flesh on the blade—how could I bear it?
translations.idiomatic: But I cannot bear to waste our people's lives on the sword. How could I?

sentences.zh: 若曹其徇眾議，紓急禍。

translations.literal: You should follow the public decision and ease this urgent calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Do as the assembly asks and ease this immediate danger.

sentences.zh: 吾身為大臣，且天潢親也，宜效死。」

translations.literal: I myself am a high minister and moreover of the imperial lineage; I ought to die in service."
translations.idiomatic: I am a high minister and of the imperial house; it is for me to die in service."

sentences.zh: 是時驍騎校萬選力爭，請毋止戰，不見用，頓足大哭。

translations.literal: At this time the valiant cavalry officer Wan Xuan argued forcefully, begging that fighting not be halted; his plea was not adopted, and he stamped his feet and wept aloud.
translations.idiomatic: The valiant cavalry officer Wan Xuan argued fiercely against yielding and pleaded that they not stop fighting, but was overruled. He stamped his feet and wept.

sentences.zh: 印班德霈亦憤甚，曰：「大局休矣！

translations.literal: The seal officer De Pei was also deeply angered and said, "The great situation is finished!
translations.idiomatic: The seal officer De Pei was furious as well. "The cause is lost," he said.

sentences.zh: 吾寧死以報國。」

translations.literal: I would rather die to repay the state."
translations.idiomatic: I would rather die for the country."

sentences.zh: 載穆嘿不語，乃繕遺疏，手自緘印，遣佐領良才賚至京師。

translations.literal: Zaimu was silent. He then drafted a final memorial, sealed it with his own hand, and sent the assistant commander Liang Cai to deliver it to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zaimu said nothing. He drafted a final memorial, sealed it himself, and sent Assistant Commander Liang Cai to bear it to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 复草遺書致商會，猶殷殷以七千人生命相囑。

translations.literal: He also drafted a farewell letter to the chamber of commerce, earnestly entrusting to them the lives of seven thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote a farewell letter to the chamber of commerce, earnestly charging them with the lives of seven thousand people.

sentences.zh: 隨行四僕皆遣歸。

translations.literal: The four servants who accompanied him were all sent home.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his four attending servants away.

sentences.zh: 有李順者，去復返，朝夕侍其側，偶退休，詰朝入寢室，則已自經死矣。

translations.literal: One Li Shun left and returned again, attending him morning and evening. Once when Li took a brief rest, at dawn he entered the bedchamber and found Zaimu had already hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: A servant named Li Shun left and came back again, waiting on him day and night. Once when Li stepped away briefly, he entered the bedroom at dawn and found Zaimu had hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 郡人哀之，殯斂如禮，且為置田安厝焉。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture mourned him, buried him with full rites, and also set aside fields for his proper interment.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the district mourned him, buried him with full rites, and set aside land for his tomb.

sentences.zh: 將軍鐵良上聞，命覈覆死事。

translations.literal: General Tie Liang reported upward, and an order was issued to verify his death in service.
translations.idiomatic: General Tie Liang reported the matter to the court, which ordered an inquiry into his death in service.

sentences.zh: 江寧失，鐵良走，宗人府亦無奏報，故褒贈之典弗及云。

translations.literal: Jiangning fell, Tie Liang fled, and the Imperial Clan Court also made no memorial report, so the posthumous honors did not reach him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangning then fell, Tie Liang fled, and the Imperial Clan Court filed no report, so the usual posthumous honors never reached him.

sentences.zh: 萬選、德霈並殉。

translations.literal: Wan Xuan and De Pei both died with him.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Xuan and De Pei died with him as well.

sentences.zh: 先是驍騎校同源以旗人將失所，忍死爭旗產。

translations.literal: Earlier the valiant cavalry officer Tong Yuan, because banner people would lose their footing, had endured death to fight for banner property.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the valiant cavalry officer Tong Yuan, fearing that banner families would lose their livelihood, had risked death to defend banner property.

sentences.zh: 至是乃語家人曰：「吾可以從殉國諸公後矣！」

translations.literal: Now he said to his family, "I may follow the gentlemen who died for the state!"
translations.idiomatic: Now he told his family, "I may follow the men who died for the dynasty."

sentences.zh: 沐浴整衣冠，不食而死。

translations.literal: He bathed, arranged cap and robes, and died by fasting.
translations.idiomatic: He bathed, dressed in his formal robes, and starved himself to death.

sentences.zh: 萬選，字子昭，蒙古敖漢氏。

translations.literal: Wan Xuan, styled Zizhao, was of the Mongol Aohan clan.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Xuan, styled Zizhao, was of the Mongol Aohan clan.

sentences.zh: 著有易注、筆諫、金石賞心、火龍攻戰略諸書。

translations.literal: He authored such works as Commentary on the Changes, Brush Admonitions, Appreciating Metal and Stone, and Fire Dragon Attack Strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Commentaries on the Changes, Brush Admonitions, Appreciating Metal and Stone, and Fire Dragon Attack Strategy, among other works.

sentences.zh: 德霈，字雨田；

translations.literal: De Pei, styled Yutian;
translations.idiomatic: De Pei, styled Yutian;

sentences.zh: 同源，字子清：並蒙古人。

translations.literal: Tong Yuan, styled Ziqing: both were Mongols.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Yuan, styled Ziqing: both were Mongols.

sentences.zh: 文瑞，鈕祜祿氏，滿洲鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: Wen Rui was of the Niohuru clan and a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Rui was of the Niohuru clan and enrolled in the Manchu Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 世襲男爵，充頭等侍衛，出為馬蘭鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He inherited the baronetcy, served as a first-class bodyguard, and went out as brigade general of Malan.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited a baron's title, served as a first-class imperial bodyguard, and was appointed brigade general at Malan.

sentences.zh: 中日之役，喜峰口迫近戰地，策守禦，遏內匪，轄境以寧。

translations.literal: In the Sino-Japanese War, Xifengkou lay close to the battlefield. He planned defenses, checked internal bandits, and his jurisdiction was thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sino-Japanese War his post at Xifengkou lay near the front. He organized defenses, suppressed local banditry, and kept his district quiet.

sentences.zh: 坐陵樹蟲災免，頃之被宥，除歸化城副都統，兼署綏遠城將軍。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for an insect plague among imperial tomb trees, but soon was pardoned and appointed vice commander at Guihuacheng, concurrently acting as general at Suiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed after insects damaged trees at the imperial tombs, but was soon pardoned and made vice commander at Guihuacheng, concurrently acting general at Suiyuan.

sentences.zh: 拳匪亂，蔓延蒙旗，教案紛糾。

translations.literal: When the Boxer turmoil arose it spread through Mongol banners and missionary cases multiplied in dispute.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer rising spread into the Mongol banners, missionary cases multiplied and relations grew tense.

sentences.zh: 文瑞至，與外人推誠商榷，償款獨輕，綏民德之。

translations.literal: When Wen Rui arrived he dealt frankly with foreigners in consultation; indemnities alone were light, and the pacified people were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Rui dealt openly with foreign representatives; the indemnities he arranged were unusually light, and the people were grateful.

sentences.zh: 調青州，念旗民乏生計，為闢工廠，興學校，編制軍隊，滿城一切皆治辦。

translations.literal: Transferred to Qingzhou, mindful that banner people lacked livelihoods, he opened factories, founded schools, reorganized the army, and put everything in the Manchu city in order.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingzhou, seeing that banner families lacked livelihoods, he opened factories, founded schools, reorganized the garrison, and put the Manchu quarter in order.

sentences.zh: 移成都，未之官，擢西安將軍。

translations.literal: He was moved to Chengdu but did not take that post and was promoted to General at Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chengdu but never took up that post and was promoted to general at Xi'an instead.

sentences.zh: 興學、勸工，為治复仿青州。

translations.literal: He promoted schools and encouraged crafts; his style of governance again followed the Qingzhou model.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted schools and crafts and governed Xi'an much as he had Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 議辦移墾授田法，未及行而鄂變作，西安新軍應之，先據漢城，緣塗縱火，煙焰張天。

translations.literal: He discussed implementing land-grant colonization laws, but before they could be carried out trouble broke out in Hubei. The new army at Xi'an responded, first seizing the Han city, setting fires along the roads until smoke and flame filled the sky.
translations.idiomatic: He was planning land-grant colonization schemes when rebellion broke out in Hubei. The new army at Xi'an joined in, seized the Han quarter first, and set fires along the streets until the sky was black with smoke.

sentences.zh: 疾趨南街，遇新軍，前騶戈什哈數人被擊死，紆道歸。

translations.literal: He hurried to South Street, met the new army, and several of his outriders and attendants were struck down and killed; he took a roundabout route back.
translations.idiomatic: He rushed to South Street, ran into the new army, and several of his escorts were killed before he made his way back by a side route.

sentences.zh: 與左翼副都統承燕、右翼副都統克蒙額籌應變策，遣軍士畫陴而守，兩軍合戰，自申及亥不少休。

translations.literal: With Left Vice Commander Cheng Yan and Right Vice Commander Ke Meng'e he planned responses to the crisis, sent soldiers to mark the ramparts and defend. The two armies joined battle from the shen hour to the hai hour without pause.
translations.idiomatic: With the left vice commander Cheng Yan and the right vice commander Ke Meng'e he planned their response, posted men along the walls, and fought the new army from mid-afternoon until late evening without respite.

sentences.zh: 翼日昧爽，新軍分攻東、南門，旗兵多傷亡，文瑞督懾益力。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day the new army attacked the eastern and southern gates in separate columns. Many banner soldiers were killed or wounded, and Wen Rui directed the defense with redoubled effort.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the next day the new army assaulted the eastern and southern gates. Banner casualties mounted, and Wen Rui drove the defense with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 未幾，新軍請停戰會議，遣協領葆鈞往，迄未得要領。

translations.literal: Before long the new army asked for a ceasefire and conference. He sent Assistant Commander Bao Jun, but no agreement was reached.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the new army asked for a truce and talks. He sent Assistant Commander Bao Jun, but no terms could be agreed.

sentences.zh: 复貽書新軍，反覆開喻，亦不答。

translations.literal: He again sent letters to the new army, repeatedly explaining and persuading, but received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote again to the new army, reasoning with them at length, but they did not answer.

sentences.zh: 而新軍又兩路夾攻，旗營火器竭，漸不支。

translations.literal: Then the new army attacked from two routes at once; the banner camp's firearms were exhausted and they gradually could not hold.
translations.idiomatic: The new army then attacked on two fronts at once. The banner garrison ran out of firearms and could no longer hold.

sentences.zh: 日方午，東門破，進滿城，終夕巷戰，旗兵死者二千餘人，餘皆屠殺。

translations.literal: At midday the eastern gate was breached and they entered the Manchu city. Street fighting lasted all night; more than two thousand banner soldiers died and the rest were slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: At noon the eastern gate fell. The rebels entered the Manchu quarter and street fighting raged all night. More than two thousand banner soldiers died; the rest were massacred.

sentences.zh: 麾下壯士從者十餘，及其子熙麟而已。

translations.literal: Only a dozen or so stalwart followers remained at his side, together with his son Xilin.
translations.idiomatic: Only a dozen loyal followers remained, together with his son Xilin.

sentences.zh: 於是環請引避圖恢復，文瑞愾然曰：「吾為統兵大員，有職守不能戡亂，重負君恩，惟有死耳！」

translations.literal: Thereupon those around him begged him to withdraw and plan recovery. Wen Rui said angrily, "I am a commander-in-chief with a duty to quell disorder. I have failed the emperor's grace; death alone remains!"
translations.idiomatic: His followers begged him to withdraw and regroup. Wen Rui said angrily, "I am a commanding general charged with putting down rebellion. I have failed the emperor; I can only die."

sentences.zh: 乃口授遺疏，趣熙麟書之，命乘間達京師，而自從​​容整衣冠赴井死。

translations.literal: He then dictated a final memorial, urging Xilin to write it, and ordered him to find an opportunity to deliver it to the capital, while he himself calmly arranged cap and robes and threw himself into a well to die.
translations.idiomatic: He dictated a final memorial for Xilin to write and told him to get it to Beijing if he could, then calmly dressed in his formal robes and drowned himself in a well.

sentences.zh: 幕僚秦鶴鳴斂之。

translations.literal: His staff member Qin Heming arranged his burial.
translations.idiomatic: His aide Qin Heming arranged his burial.

sentences.zh: 承燕同時投井死。

translations.literal: Cheng Yan at the same time threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yan drowned himself in a well at the same time.

sentences.zh: 克蒙額，字哲臣，滿洲鑲藍旗人。

translations.literal: Ke Meng'e, styled Zhechen, was a Manchu of the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Meng'e, styled Zhechen, was a Manchu of the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 先請巡撫發新式軍械，遲不應，激戰三晝夜，力竭陣亡。

translations.literal: He had first asked the governor to issue new-style arms, but the response was delayed. After fierce fighting for three days and nights his strength was spent and he fell on the field.
translations.idiomatic: He had asked the governor for modern arms, but help came too late. After three days and nights of fierce fighting his strength gave out and he was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 恆齡，字錫九，舒穆魯氏，滿洲正藍旗人，湖北荊州駐防。

translations.literal: Heng Ling, styled Xijiu, was of the Shumulu clan, a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner, garrisoned at Jingzhou in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Heng Ling, styled Xijiu, was of the Shumulu clan, enrolled in the Manchu Plain Blue Banner, and garrisoned at Jingzhou in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 恆齡少嗜學，嫺武幹，尤熟中外兵家言。

translations.literal: Heng Ling from youth loved study, was skilled in military affairs, and was especially versed in Chinese and foreign writings on war.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Heng Ling loved learning, was skilled in military affairs, and knew both Chinese and Western military theory well.

sentences.zh: 以附生官筆帖式，遷驍騎校，累擢佐領。

translations.literal: As a licentiate he became a clerical secretary, was transferred to valiant cavalry officer, and was promoted in succession to assistant commander.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a licentiate clerk, he rose to valiant cavalry officer and then to assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 旗營久習窳惰，罕知兵事，乃創編新軍，設講武堂教之。

translations.literal: The banner camp had long been habituated to slackness and rarely knew military affairs. He therefore organized a new army and established a military academy to train them.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison had grown slack and knew little of soldiering, so he formed a new force and opened a military academy to train them.

sentences.zh: 拳匪亂作，湘人旅荊者被煽動，燔沙市躉船及稅關、領事署，外國僑民多逃避，勢岌岌。

translations.literal: When the Boxer turmoil arose, Hunanese residing at Jingzhou were incited to burn wholesale boats at Shashi and the tax office and consulate. Many foreign residents fled; the situation was perilous.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer rising broke out, Hunanese in Jingzhou were stirred up to burn warehouses at Shashi along with the customs house and consulate. Foreign residents fled and the situation looked desperate.

sentences.zh: 恆齡率二百人往鎮撫，誅首要，宥脅從，外人避難者護持之。

translations.literal: Heng Ling led two hundred men to pacify the region, executed the ringleaders, pardoned those coerced, and protected foreigners seeking refuge.
translations.idiomatic: Heng Ling led two hundred men to restore order, executed the ringleaders, pardoned those who had been coerced, and protected foreigners who sought refuge.

sentences.zh: 事寧，軍政課最。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled his military administration ranked highest.
translations.idiomatic: When order was restored his military administration received the highest rating.

sentences.zh: 將軍綽哈布疏綜營務，恆齡條上四事，曰：設警察，興學校，釐財政，練常備軍，並奏行。

translations.literal: General Chuo Habu memorialized on overall camp affairs. Heng Ling itemized four matters: establish police, found schools, regulate finances, and drill a standing army—all were memorialized and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: General Chuo Habu reported on garrison affairs. Heng Ling proposed four measures—police, schools, fiscal reform, and a standing army—and all were adopted.

sentences.zh: 設八旗高等學堂、陸軍小學堂，俾任校事。

translations.literal: He established a Banner Higher School and an Army Primary School and was put in charge of both.
translations.idiomatic: He founded a banner higher school and an army primary school and was placed in charge of both.

sentences.zh: 顧其時風氣闇僿，款無所出，遂走謁總督張之洞，面陳規畫，獲助萬金，始成立；

translations.literal: But the climate of the time was benighted and close-minded, and funds were nowhere to be found. He therefore went in person to visit Governor-General Zhang Zhidong, stated his plans face to face, received ten thousand taels in aid, and only then could they be established;
translations.idiomatic: Funds were scarce and local opinion was narrow, so he went in person to Governor-General Zhang Zhidong, laid out his plans, and received ten thousand taels before the schools could open;

sentences.zh: 猶不足，省新軍陋規益之，歲以為常。

translations.literal: still it was not enough, so he cut wasteful practices of the provincial new army to supplement them, making this an annual practice.
translations.idiomatic: even that was not enough, so he trimmed waste from the provincial new army's budget each year to make up the shortfall.

sentences.zh: 於是訂章條，甄材穎，走書幣聘海內名儒，分科教授，校風肅然。

translations.literal: Thereupon he drew up regulations, selected talented students, sent letters and gifts to recruit renowned scholars from throughout the realm for instruction by subject, and school discipline was strict.
translations.idiomatic: He drew up regulations, selected promising students, and recruited distinguished scholars from across the country to teach by subject. Discipline at the schools was exemplary.

sentences.zh: 學部曹司考察，稱荊州第一。

translations.literal: When the Ministry of Education's clerks inspected, they ranked Jingzhou first.
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors from the ministry of education ranked Jingzhou first in the province.

sentences.zh: 旋領振威新軍，調督練處參議，總辦陸軍小學。

translations.literal: Soon he commanded the Zhenwei New Army, was transferred as adviser to the training directorate, and oversaw the army primary school.
translations.idiomatic: He soon commanded the Zhenwei New Army, became an adviser at the training directorate, and oversaw the army primary school.

sentences.zh: 將軍恩存、總督陳夔龍交章論薦。

translations.literal: General En Cun and Governor Chen Kuilong submitted joint memorials recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: General En Cun and Governor Chen Kuilong jointly recommended him in memorials.

sentences.zh: 宣統改元，調充熱河練軍統領。

translations.literal: At the change of reign to Xuantong he was transferred to command the Rehe training army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xuantong reign he was appointed to command the Rehe training army.

sentences.zh: 汰老弱，補缺額，申嚴紀律，凡兩閱月，獲匪首葛蘭亭等，推功將校。

translations.literal: He eliminated the old and weak, filled vacant quotas, and enforced discipline strictly. Within two months he captured bandit chiefs Ge Lanting and others, crediting officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He cut the old and weak from the rolls, filled vacancies, and enforced strict discipline. Within two months he captured the bandit chief Ge Lanting and others, giving credit to his officers and men.

sentences.zh: 二年，授寧夏副都統，朝陽紳民籥留，夔龍上聞。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed vice commander at Ningxia. Gentry and people of Chaoyang petitioned to retain him; Kuilong reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: In 1910 he was appointed vice commander at Ningxia. The gentry of Chaoyang petitioned to keep him, and Kuilong reported this to the court.

sentences.zh: 廷議以西陲邊要，趣到官。

translations.literal: Court deliberation held that the western frontier was vital and urged him to take office promptly.
translations.idiomatic: The court decided the western frontier was too important and ordered him to take up his post at once.

sentences.zh: 既蒞事，首嚴煙禁；

translations.literal: Once he assumed duties he first enforced strict prohibition of opium;
translations.idiomatic: On taking office his first measure was a strict ban on opium;

sentences.zh: 開渠屯田，久無效，設方略整飭之。

translations.literal: Canal opening and frontier farming had long been ineffective; he devised measures to reorganize them.
translations.idiomatic: he reorganized long-neglected canal and frontier-farming projects.

sentences.zh: 三年，遭父憂。

translations.literal: In the third year he suffered his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: In 1911 his father died.

sentences.zh: 令甲，旗員百日服除即視事。

translations.literal: By regulation, banner members after a hundred days of mourning were to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations required banner officers to resume duty after a hundred days of mourning.

sentences.zh: 恆齡固請終制，解職去，奉父喪於萬縣，抵宜昌，鄂亂作，道塗阻絕，將軍連魁疏請參軍事，上命署荊州左翼副都統。

translations.literal: Heng Ling firmly asked to complete the full mourning period, resigned his post, and conducted his father's funeral at Wanxian. Reaching Yichang, turmoil broke out in Hubei and roads were cut off. General Lian Kui memorialized asking him to take part in military affairs, and the throne ordered him to act as left vice commander at Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Heng Ling insisted on observing the full mourning period, resigned, and buried his father at Wanxian. At Yichang rebellion broke out in Hubei and travel became impossible. General Lian Kui asked the court to use him militarily, and he was ordered to act as left vice commander at Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 恆齡援「墨絰從戎」義，愾然任城守，而援絕餉匱，兵人疲饉則譁變，乃斥家財餉之，涕泣誓眾，令毋擾沙市啟外釁。

translations.literal: Heng Ling invoked the principle of "mourning garb in campaign," took up city defense with indignation, but aid was cut off and provisions exhausted. When troops were weary and hungry they mutinied; he then spent his family wealth to pay them, wept and swore before the masses, and ordered that Shashi not be disturbed to provoke foreign trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Invoking the tradition of "taking the field in mourning dress," he angrily undertook the city's defense. Relief and supplies ran out; when hungry troops mutinied he spent his family fortune to pay them, wept before his men, and ordered that Shashi be left unmolested lest foreigners be provoked.

sentences.zh: 時方患癰劇，裹創策騎出，晝夜徼循，血痕猶濡縷然。

translations.literal: At the time he was suffering from a severe boil. Binding his wound he rode out on patrol day and night, blood still soaking his garments in threads.
translations.idiomatic: He was suffering from a severe abscess but rode out day and night with his wound bound, blood still seeping through his clothes.

sentences.zh: 無何，事益亟，外城失。

translations.literal: Before long the situation grew more urgent and the outer city was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the crisis worsened and the outer city fell.

sentences.zh: 恆齡晨起，公服端坐堂上，發手槍洞胸而歾。

translations.literal: Heng Ling rose in the morning, sat in official dress upright in the hall, fired a pistol through his chest, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Heng Ling rose in the morning, put on his official robes, sat upright in the hall, and shot himself through the chest.

sentences.zh: 家人得其與弟恆廣、子裕文書，曰：「吾家世受國恩，宜竭力圖報。

translations.literal: His family found his letter to his younger brother Heng Guang and son Yuwen, saying, "Our family has received the state's grace for generations and ought to repay it with all our strength.
translations.idiomatic: His family found letters to his brother Heng Guang and son Yuwen saying, "Our family has enjoyed the dynasty's favor for generations and ought to repay it with all our strength.

sentences.zh: 今城既失，義當死。

translations.literal: Now that the city is lost, by right I should die.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the city is lost, I am bound to die.

sentences.zh: 所憾者老母在堂，忠孝不獲兩全。

translations.literal: What I regret is that my aged mother is still living; loyalty and filial piety cannot both be fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: My only regret is that my mother still lives; I cannot fulfill both loyalty and filial duty.

sentences.zh: 第吾母有子能盡忠，亦甚得。

translations.literal: Yet my mother has a son who can exhaust his loyalty—that is also very fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Yet she has a son who can die loyal—that should comfort her somewhat.

sentences.zh: 我死，汝曹能闔門殉節固善，否則善事吾母，以補吾不孝之罪，毋以吾死狀令老人知也。」

translations.literal: When I die, if you can all die together in loyalty to the dynasty, that is well; otherwise serve my mother well to make up for my unfilial offense, and do not let the old lady know the manner of my death."
translations.idiomatic: After I die, if you can all die with me, so much the better; otherwise care for my mother and atone for my unfilial conduct, and do not let her know how I died."

sentences.zh: 恆齡死數日，連魁與右翼副都統松鶴開門納民軍，荊州遂失。

translations.literal: Several days after Heng Ling's death, Lian Kui and Right Vice Commander Song He opened the gates and admitted the revolutionary army; Jingzhou was thereby lost.
translations.idiomatic: A few days after Heng Ling's death, Lian Kui and the right vice commander Song He opened the gates to the revolutionary army, and Jingzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 事聞，上震悼，諡壯節。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported the emperor was shaken with grief and gave the posthumous name Zhuangjie.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne the court was shaken with grief and gave him the posthumous name Zhuangjie, "Steadfast in Integrity."

sentences.zh: 參謀長德霈自經死。

translations.literal: Chief of staff De Pei hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: His chief of staff, De Pei, hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 恩霈亦自經，家人救之，憤不欲生，後數日卒。

translations.literal: En Pei also tried to hang himself; his family saved him, but in anger he wished not to live and died several days later.
translations.idiomatic: En Pei also tried to hang himself. His family saved him, but grief consumed him and he died a few days later.

sentences.zh: 樸壽，字仁山，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Pu Shou, styled Renshan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Shou, styled Renshan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十年舉人，授吏部主事，累遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Guangxu he passed the provincial examination, was appointed a director in the Ministry of Personnel, and was promoted in succession to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894 he passed the provincial examination, joined the ministry of personnel as a director, and rose to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 拳亂起，聯軍入城，首與各國謀保商民。

translations.literal: When the Boxer turmoil arose and the allied armies entered the city, he was the first to consult with the various powers on protecting merchants and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxers rose and allied troops entered Beijing, he was among the first to negotiate with the foreign powers to protect merchants and civilians.

sentences.zh: 出為山西歸綏道，簡庫倫辦事大臣。

translations.literal: He went out as intendant of Guihua circuit in Shanxi and was selected as minister in charge at Urga.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as intendant of Guihua in Shanxi and later selected as minister in charge at Urga.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，召授鑲藍旗滿洲副都統，遷正黃旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was summoned and appointed Manchu vice commander of the Bordered Blue Banner, then transferred to commander of the Chinese Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1906 he was recalled and made Manchu vice commander of the Bordered Blue Banner, then commander of the Chinese Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 明年，除福州將軍，整旗務，嚴煙禁，專志訓練，得精卒四千人。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed General at Fuzhou, put banner affairs in order, enforced strict opium prohibition, devoted himself solely to training, and obtained four thousand elite soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed general at Fuzhou, reorganized banner affairs, banned opium, concentrated on training, and built a force of four thousand elite troops.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年，省城民軍起，率防軍與搏，火器猛利，民軍幾不支。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuantong the provincial capital's revolutionary army rose. He led the defense force to fight them; their firearms were fierce and effective, and the revolutionary army nearly could not hold.
translations.idiomatic: In 1911 the revolutionary army rose in the provincial capital. He led the defense garrison into battle; his troops' firepower was so strong the revolutionaries nearly broke.

sentences.zh: 然民軍雖被創，輒隨時募集，防軍以猛鬥故，傷亡多，卒敗潰。

translations.literal: Yet though the revolutionary army suffered wounds, they recruited anew at once. Because the defense force fought fiercely its casualties were many, and in the end it was defeated and routed.
translations.idiomatic: Though wounded, the revolutionaries recruited replacements at once. Pu Shou's troops fought fiercely but took heavy losses and were finally routed.

sentences.zh: 樸壽被執，受挫辱，不屈，遂支解之，棄屍山下，其死狀為最烈云。

translations.literal: Pu Shou was seized, suffered abuse, and would not yield. He was thereupon dismembered and his corpse cast below the hill; his manner of death was the most brutal.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Shou was captured and humiliated but would not submit. He was dismembered and his body thrown below the hill—the most brutal death in the chapter.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈太子太保，予二等輕車都尉世職，諡忠肅。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted a hereditary second-class commandery chariot captaincy, and given the posthumous name Zhongsu.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted a hereditary second-class commandery chariot captaincy, and gave him the posthumous name Zhongsu, "Loyal and Stern."

sentences.zh: 謝寶勝，字子蘭，安徽壽州人。

translations.literal: Xie Baosheng, styled Zilan, was a native of Shouzhou in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Baosheng, styled Zilan, was from Shouzhou in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 初隸金順麾下，從征西陲。

translations.literal: At first he served under Jin Shun and campaigned on the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He first served under Jin Shun on campaigns in the far west.

sentences.zh: 嗣隨宋慶、馬玉昆克肅州及關外諸城，積勳至都司。

translations.literal: Later he followed Song Qing and Ma Yukun in capturing Suzhou and cities beyond the pass, accumulating merit until he reached the rank of colonel.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Song Qing and Ma Yukun in taking Suzhou and other cities beyond the pass and rose to colonel on accumulated merit.

sentences.zh: 以事與玉昆左，棄冠服走博克達山為黃冠。

translations.literal: Because of a dispute with Yukun he cast off cap and robes, fled to Mount Bogda, and became a Daoist priest.
translations.idiomatic: After a falling-out with Ma Yukun he abandoned his office, fled to Mount Bogda, and became a Daoist priest.

sentences.zh: 光緒十五年，玉昆提督畿輔，鳩集舊部，獨偉視寶勝，招之出。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Guangxu, Yukun became governor-general of the metropolitan region, gathered his old troops, and alone held Baosheng in high regard, summoning him forth.
translations.idiomatic: In 1889 Ma Yukun became governor-general of Zhili, reassembled his old command, singled out Baosheng for special regard, and called him back to service.

sentences.zh: 敦促備至，寶勝愾然曰：「玉昆知我者，義不忍卻！」

translations.literal: His urging was extreme. Baosheng said angrily, "Yukun is one who knows me—I cannot in honor refuse!"
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yukun pressed him insistently. Baosheng said angrily, "Yukun knows me well—I cannot in honor refuse!"

sentences.zh: 乃棄黃冠，詣軍所獻方略。

translations.literal: He then cast off the Daoist robe, went to the army camp, and presented strategic plans.
translations.idiomatic: He laid aside his priest's robes, went to headquarters, and offered his plans.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，朝鮮告警，從出關，與日軍數十戰，勇敢躐倫等。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year alarm arose in Korea; he followed beyond the pass and fought the Japanese army in dozens of battles, his bravery surpassing his peers.
translations.idiomatic: In 1895, when war broke out in Korea, he crossed the frontier and fought the Japanese in dozens of engagements, his courage unmatched among his peers.

sentences.zh: 玉昆弟陷重圍，銳身救之出。

translations.literal: Yukun's younger brother was trapped in a heavy encirclement; Baosheng boldly went in and rescued him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Yukun's younger brother was surrounded, Baosheng fought his way in and brought him out.

sentences.zh: 和議成，憤甚，復為道士裝，羈跡京師白雲觀，如是者數年。

translations.literal: When peace was concluded he was deeply angry, again took Daoist dress, and lingered at the White Cloud Abbey in the capital for several years.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was made he was furious, put on Daoist robes again, and lived for years at the White Cloud Abbey in Beijing.

sentences.zh: 拳亂作，柴洪山統武衛護軍，榮祿檄領前路後營，已留河南，更名精銳軍，領左營，尋筦豫北軍。

translations.literal: When the Boxer turmoil arose, Chai Hongshan commanded the Wuwei Guard. Ronglu ordered him to lead the rear camp of the forward route, already stationed in Henan, renamed the Elite Army, commanded the Left Battalion, and soon took charge of northern Henan forces.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxers rose, Chai Hongshan commanded the Wuwei Guard. Ronglu ordered Baosheng to lead a rear battalion in Henan; the unit was renamed the Elite Army, and he soon took command of forces in northern Henan.

sentences.zh: 忌者中以蜚語，巡撫吳重憙疏辨其冤，上卒優容之。

translations.literal: Envious men spread slander against him. Governor Wu Chongxi memorialized to clear his name, and the throne at last treated him leniently.
translations.idiomatic: Rivals spread rumors against him, but Governor Wu Chongxi memorialized in his defense and the court eventually exonerated him.

sentences.zh: 駐軍河、陝、汝最久，將士積相畏服，軍麾所指，紀律肅然。

translations.literal: He garrisoned the He, Shan, and Ru regions longest. Officers and soldiers came over time to fear and respect him; wherever his banner pointed, discipline was strict.
translations.idiomatic: He was longest stationed along the He, Shan, and Ru rivers. His officers and men came to respect and fear him, and wherever his banner pointed discipline held firm.

sentences.zh: 累遷至副將。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to brigade deputy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to brigade deputy.

sentences.zh: 宣統改元，授河北鎮總兵。

translations.literal: At the change of reign to Xuantong he was appointed brigade general of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xuantong reign he was appointed brigade general of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 明年，移南陽，河、陝、汝軍仍受節度。

translations.literal: The next year he was moved to Nanyang; forces of the He, Shan, and Ru still came under his command.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to Nanyang while still commanding the He, Shan, and Ru forces.

sentences.zh: 寶勝益感奮，尤嚴治盜，所蒞毌擾民。

translations.literal: Baosheng was all the more stirred to effort, especially strict in suppressing bandits; wherever he took post he never troubled the people.
translations.idiomatic: Baosheng threw himself into the work, cracked down hard on banditry, and never allowed his troops to harass civilians.

sentences.zh: 恆短衣執械先士卒，或宵行數十百里，偽為小商，诇虛實。

translations.literal: He constantly wore short dress, took arms, and led before the soldiers; sometimes he traveled scores of li by night, disguised as a petty merchant to spy out conditions.
translations.idiomatic: He often wore plain clothes, took up arms, and led from the front; sometimes he traveled scores of miles by night disguised as a peddler to scout the enemy.

sentences.zh: 村民通匪者憚其至，嘗置毒飲水處，寶勝則自攜水罂，懷麥餅，食盡，忍飢渴以為常，以是寇鮮漏網。

translations.literal: Villagers who communicated with bandits feared his arrival and sometimes placed poison at drinking places. Baosheng carried his own water jar and wheat cakes in his bosom; when food was gone he endured hunger and thirst as routine, and thus bandits rarely escaped the net.
translations.idiomatic: Villages that colluded with bandits feared him and sometimes poisoned water sources. He carried his own water jar and wheat cakes and routinely endured hunger and thirst on campaign, so few bandits escaped him.

sentences.zh: 洛陽張黑子、嵩縣王天縱、汝州董萬川尤鷙悍，張、董併計擒之，天縱懼不敢出。

translations.literal: Zhang Heizi of Luoyang, Wang Tianzong of Songxian, and Dong Wanchuan of Ruzhou were especially fierce. Zhang and Dong were captured together by stratagem; Tianzong in fear dared not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heizi of Luoyang, Wang Tianzong of Songxian, and Dong Wanchuan of Ruzhou were especially fierce. He captured Zhang and Dong by stratagem; Tianzong was too afraid to show himself.

sentences.zh: 豫西數十州縣皆安堵，而南陽王八老虎猶嵎負。

translations.literal: Several dozen prefectures and counties in western Henan were all settled, but Wang Balao of Nanyang still crouched defiant.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of counties in western Henan were pacified, but Wang Balao of Nanyang still held out defiantly.

sentences.zh: 寶勝至，移書期決鬥。

translations.literal: When Baosheng arrived he sent a letter fixing a day for decisive combat.
translations.idiomatic: When Baosheng arrived he sent a letter challenging Wang to a decisive fight.

sentences.zh: 會天大雪，前期五日，潛師薄其巢，賊不戒，據中庭轟拒。

translations.literal: It happened that heavy snow fell. Five days before the appointed time he secretly led troops close to their lair. The bandits were unwary but, holding the central courtyard, fired back in a roar.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow fell. Five days before the appointed duel he led troops secretly to the bandits' lair. They were caught off guard but fought back fiercely from the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 寶勝奮身入，眾繼之，火其廬，卒就縛，置之法。

translations.literal: Baosheng rushed in bodily; the masses followed, burned their huts, and in the end they were bound and brought to justice.
translations.idiomatic: Baosheng charged in himself; his men followed, burned the camp, captured Wang, and executed him by law.

sentences.zh: 自是南陽無遺寇。

translations.literal: From then on Nanyang had no remaining bandits.
translations.idiomatic: After that no bandits remained in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 寶勝短軀幹，目光炯炯能懾人。

translations.literal: Baosheng was short in stature, his eyes bright and piercing enough to awe men.
translations.idiomatic: Baosheng was short in stature, but his bright, piercing gaze could intimidate anyone.

sentences.zh: 視盜如仇，待士卒若子弟。

translations.literal: He regarded bandits as enemies and treated soldiers like sons and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He hated bandits as personal enemies and treated his soldiers like family.

sentences.zh: 勞無吝賞，遇喪亡，賻卹尤厚。

translations.literal: For labor he never stinted rewards; when death occurred his condolence payments were especially generous.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded hard work generously and gave especially rich condolence payments when men fell.

sentences.zh: 餉饋無所受，無兼衣餘食，統兵十餘年，而負債鉅萬。

translations.literal: He accepted no gifts of provisions, had no spare garments or leftover food, commanded troops for more than ten years, yet owed tens of thousands in debt.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted no gifts, owned no spare clothes or extra food, commanded troops for more than ten years, and still owed tens of thousands of taels.

sentences.zh: 巡撫寶棻上聞，中旨敕司庫償九千餘金，異數也！

translations.literal: Governor Bao Fen reported upward; an imperial rescript ordered the treasury to repay more than nine thousand taels—an extraordinary favor!
translations.idiomatic: Governor Bao Fen reported his case to the throne, and an imperial order directed the treasury to repay more than nine thousand taels—an exceptional act of grace.

sentences.zh: 三年，移師嵩縣。

translations.literal: In the third year he moved his forces to Songxian.
translations.idiomatic: In 1911 he moved his troops to Songxian.

sentences.zh: 值鄂亂作，亟還籌戰守。

translations.literal: When turmoil broke out in Hubei he hurried back to plan offense and defense.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion broke out in Hubei he rushed back to plan how to fight and hold his ground.

sentences.zh: 其時襄樊已應和，土寇處處飆起。

translations.literal: At that time Xiangyang and Fancheng had already responded in sympathy, and local bandits rose everywhere like whirlwinds.
translations.idiomatic: By then Xiangyang and Fancheng had joined the uprising, and local bandits were rising everywhere.

sentences.zh: 豫南與陝、鄂壤地接，市言訛鷖日數至。

translations.literal: Southern Henan bordered Shaanxi and Hubei, and market rumors and false reports arrived daily in numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Henan bordered Shaanxi and Hubei, and rumors and alarming reports arrived every day.

sentences.zh: 檢勒部曲，日夕巡徼不少休。

translations.literal: He inspected and restrained his troops, patrolling day and night without rest.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled his troops and patrolled day and night without rest.

sentences.zh: 支振數十日，而襄樊軍闌入，士民與通款，將內訌。

translations.literal: He held out for several tens of days, but Xiang-Fan forces forced their way in; soldiers and civilians communicated with them and internal strife was about to break out.
translations.idiomatic: He held on for several weeks, but Xiangyang-Fancheng troops broke in; his men and local people were in contact with them and mutiny was imminent.

sentences.zh: 諸將意沮，咸莫能奮，惟都司姚靄雲慷慨原從戰。

translations.literal: The generals' spirits were damped; none could rouse themselves to fight—only Colonel Yao Aiyun generously volunteered to follow into battle.
translations.idiomatic: His officers lost heart and none would fight—only Colonel Yao Aiyun volunteered to stand with him.

sentences.zh: 無何，新野陷，大吏飛檄戒毋妄動。

translations.literal: Before long Xinye fell, and high officials sent urgent dispatches warning against rash movement.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xinye fell, and superiors sent urgent orders warning him not to act rashly.

sentences.zh: 寶勝憤激，赴校場，與眾誓死守，而府縣官已委印綬去。

translations.literal: Baosheng was furious and went to the drill ground, swearing with the masses to defend to the death, while prefectural and county officials had already surrendered their seals and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Baosheng, furious, went to the drill ground and swore with his men to hold to the death, while prefectural and county officials had already abandoned their posts.

sentences.zh: 翌日元旦，獨朝服詣萬壽宮行禮，痛哭不能止。

translations.literal: The next day was New Year's Day. Alone in court dress he went to the Palace of Longevity to perform rites and wept without cease.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day he went alone in court dress to the Palace of Longevity to perform the rites and wept without stopping.

sentences.zh: 俄傳南軍入，煙焰翳天，各營亦以食盡而潰。

translations.literal: Soon word came that southern forces had entered; smoke and flame veiled the sky, and each camp also broke up for lack of food.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that southern troops had entered the city; smoke blotted out the sky, and the camps broke up one by one as provisions ran out.

sentences.zh: 不得已，退頓裕州，比至，城皆樹白幟矣，乃止舍。

translations.literal: With no alternative he withdrew and encamped at Yuzhou. When he arrived, the city had already raised white banners, and he stopped there.
translations.idiomatic: He had no choice but to withdraw to Yuzhou. When he arrived, the city had already raised white flags of surrender, and he halted there.

sentences.zh: 至夕而遜位詔至，召將卒勵以忠義，麾之去，夜半時，屏僕從，肅衣冠，嘔血數升，以槍自擊死。

translations.literal: By evening the abdication edict arrived. He summoned officers and soldiers, exhorted them with loyalty and righteousness, and waved them away. At midnight he dismissed servants, arranged cap and robes, vomited several sheng of blood, and shot himself dead.
translations.idiomatic: That evening the abdication edict arrived. He assembled his officers and men, urged them to loyalty, and sent them away. At midnight he dismissed his attendants, dressed in his formal robes, vomited blood, and shot himself.

sentences.zh: 平旦，將卒趨視，皆哭失聲，以大纛裹屍，舁至獨頭鎮斂之。

translations.literal: At dawn officers and soldiers rushed to see; all wept aloud beyond control. They wrapped the corpse in a great banner and carried it to Dutou Town for burial.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn his officers and men came running; all wept aloud. They wrapped his body in his command banner and carried it to Dutou for burial.

sentences.zh: 姚靄雲，陝西人。

translations.literal: Yao Aiyun was a native of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Aiyun was from Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 舊為多隆阿部將，後從寶勝軍，隸營務處，亦為民軍所戕云。

translations.literal: He had formerly been an officer under Duolong'a, later followed Baosheng's army, and was attached to the camp affairs office. He too was killed by the revolutionary army.
translations.idiomatic: He had served under Duolong'a and later under Baosheng at the camp affairs office. He too was killed by revolutionary troops.

sentences.zh: 黃忠浩，字澤生，湖南黔陽人。

translations.literal: Huang Zhonghao, styled Zesheng, was a native of Qianyang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zhonghao, styled Zesheng, was from Qianyang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 通經術，嗜讀儒先性理書。

translations.literal: He was versed in the classics and loved to read Neo-Confucian works on nature and principle by earlier masters.
translations.idiomatic: He was versed in the classics and devoted to Neo-Confucian moral philosophy.

sentences.zh: 以優貢生入貲為內閣中書。

translations.literal: As an outstanding tribute student he purchased entry as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: As an outstanding tribute student he purchased a post as secretary in the grand secretariat.

sentences.zh: 主沅州講席，銳意地方利弊，建西路師範學堂，勸民植桑育蠶，尤顓志礦業。

translations.literal: He headed the lecture chair at Yuanzhou, devoted himself keenly to local advantages and harms, founded the Western Circuit Normal School, urged the people to plant mulberry and raise silkworms, and was especially intent on mining.
translations.idiomatic: He taught at Yuanzhou, focused on local welfare, founded the Western Circuit Normal School, encouraged sericulture, and was especially devoted to mining.

sentences.zh: 陳寶箴、趙爾巽先後撫湘，設礦局及公司，採平江金礦、常寧水口山鉛礦，至今稱厚利，皆其謀也。

translations.literal: Chen Baozhen and Zhao Erxun in succession governed Hunan, established mining bureaus and companies, and worked the Pingjiang gold mines and Changning Shuikoushan lead mines—still called highly profitable to this day—all from his planning.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Baozhen and Zhao Erxun governed Hunan in turn, they set up mining offices and companies and opened the Pingjiang gold mines and Changning Shuikoushan lead mines—still regarded as highly profitable—all on his advice.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十一年，以東事籌防，募鄉勇五百人入鄂，守田家鎮砲台。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Guangxu, because of eastern affairs and defense planning, he recruited five hundred local militia into Hubei to guard the Tianjiazhen batteries.
translations.idiomatic: In 1895, as war with Japan loomed, he raised five hundred local militia and sent them into Hubei to guard the batteries at Tianjiazhen.

sentences.zh: 總督張之洞一見重之，調領武靖營，駐洪山。

translations.literal: Governor-General Zhang Zhidong valued him at first sight and transferred him to command the Wujing Camp, stationed at Hongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Zhang Zhidong took to him at once and put him in command of the Wujing Camp at Hongshan.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，治軍長沙，統毅字軍，軍故徵苗舊旅，日久窳敝，不可用。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he trained troops at Changsha and commanded the Yi-character Army—troops formerly used against the Miao, long decayed and useless.
translations.idiomatic: In 1897 he drilled troops at Changsha and commanded the Yi Army—veteran anti-Miao forces that had grown rotten with age and were no longer fit for service.

sentences.zh: 寶箴納其議，別募威字新軍，俾主之。

translations.literal: Baozhen accepted his proposal, separately recruited the Wei-character New Army, and had him command it.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen accepted his advice, raised a new Wei Army separately, and put him in command.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，之洞檄募師勤王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year Zhidong ordered by dispatch that he recruit troops to rescue the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900 Zhang Zhidong ordered him to raise troops for the relief of the court.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，徙駐岳州，緝新堤土寇，平之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he moved station to Yuezhou, suppressed local bandits at Xindi, and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1902 he was posted to Yuezhou, suppressed bandits at Xindi, and restored order.

sentences.zh: 再入貲為道員。

translations.literal: He again purchased entry as a circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He again purchased the rank of circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 赴日本參觀大操，歸，益詳練戰術，知兵名大著。

translations.literal: He went to Japan to observe the grand maneuvers; on return he was all the more practiced in tactics, and his reputation as a military expert grew great.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Japan to observe army maneuvers and returned with a far sharper grasp of modern tactics; his reputation as a military expert spread widely.

sentences.zh: 明年，爾巽檄綜湖南營務處，統忠字旗五營。

translations.literal: The next year Erxun ordered by dispatch that he oversee the Hunan camp affairs office and command five battalions of the Zhong-character Banner.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Erxun put him in charge of the Hunan camp affairs office and five battalions of the Zhong Banner.

sentences.zh: 其冬，母憂去職。

translations.literal: That winter he left office on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he resigned to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，廣西降匪陸亞發陷柳州，湘邊大震。

translations.literal: After a year the surrendered bandit Lu Yafa of Guangxi seized Liuzhou, and the Hunan border was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: A year later the surrendered bandit Lu Yafa of Guangxi seized Liuzhou, throwing the Hunan border into alarm.

sentences.zh: 起忠浩率所部援桂，直搗梅寨，用少擊眾，寇大創，降敕褒嘉。

translations.literal: Zhonghao was recalled to lead his troops to aid Guangxi, struck straight at Meizhai, used few to strike many, inflicted heavy wounds on the bandits, and an edict of commendation was issued.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghao was recalled to lead his men into Guangxi, struck Meizhai directly, defeated a larger force with fewer troops, and received an edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 寇奔福祿村，村故瑤地，箐壑深岨，中有危塗垂線縷，容一人行。

translations.literal: The bandits fled to Fulu Village, formerly Yao territory with deep ravines and steep gorges, where a perilous path hung like a thread, allowing only one man to pass.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits fled to Fulu Village in former Yao country, where deep ravines held a perilous path no wider than a thread that only one man could traverse at a time.

sentences.zh: 忠浩乃短衣芒蹻，徒步深入。

translations.literal: Zhonghao then wore short dress and straw sandals and went in on foot deep within.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghao put on plain clothes and straw sandals and went in on foot.

sentences.zh: 會天酷暑，鬱為瘴癘，兵士死相繼，忠浩亦遘膨疾，然治軍勤如故，寇卒不敢近。

translations.literal: It happened that the weather was fiercely hot and miasma gathered; soldiers died one after another. Zhonghao also contracted swelling illness, yet he drilled the army diligently as before, and the bandits in the end dared not approach.
translations.idiomatic: The heat was fierce and miasma spread; soldiers died in succession. Zhonghao fell ill with swelling disease but drilled his men as diligently as ever, and the bandits dared not approach.

sentences.zh: 捷上，授狼山鎮總兵，請終制，改署任道員授總戎，特例也。

translations.literal: When victory was reported he was appointed brigade general of Langshan, asked to complete mourning, and was changed to acting intendant with command of troops—a special case.
