translations.idiomatic: After his victory was reported he was appointed brigade general of Langshan. Though still in mourning, he was given acting rank as intendant and field command—an exceptional arrangement.

sentences.zh: 是時岑春煊駐桂林，檄與議軍事，奏署右江鎮。

translations.literal: At this time Cen Chunxuan was stationed at Guilin, summoned him by dispatch to discuss military affairs, and memorialized him as acting commander of the Right River.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Chunxuan was then at Guilin; he summoned Zhonghao to discuss strategy and memorialized him as acting commander of the Right River.

sentences.zh: 服闋，予實授。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was given substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he received a substantive appointment.

sentences.zh: 未幾，乞假去。

translations.literal: Before long he asked leave and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he asked for leave and departed.

sentences.zh: 再至湖北，爾巽留綜營務處，兼統全省防軍，荊襄水師受節度。

translations.literal: He went again to Hubei; Erxun retained him to oversee the camp affairs office, concurrently commanded the province's defense forces, and the Jing-Xiang naval force came under his direction.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Hubei; Erxun kept him at the camp affairs office, put him in command of the provincial defense forces, and placed the Jing-Xiang naval force under his orders.

sentences.zh: 宣統二年，從爾巽入川，署提督，乞歸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuantong he followed Erxun into Sichuan, was appointed acting provincial commander, and asked to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1910 he followed Erxun into Sichuan as acting provincial commander and then asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 三年，京師開全國教育會，忠浩與焉。

translations.literal: In the third year a national education conference was opened in the capital; Zhonghao took part.
translations.idiomatic: In 1911 a national education conference met in Beijing; Zhonghao attended.

sentences.zh: 爭鐵路國有為非計，議大濬洞庭湖，紓湘菑，議論侃侃無所撓。

translations.literal: He argued that nationalization of the railways was a mistaken policy, proposed greatly dredging Dongting Lake to relieve Hunan's flood disasters, and spoke forthrightly without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that railway nationalization was a mistake, urged a major dredging of Dongting Lake to ease Hunan's floods, and spoke his mind without flinching.

sentences.zh: 還長沙，值巡撫余誠格新蒞官，黨人謀日亟。

translations.literal: Returning to Changsha, it happened that Governor Yu Chengge had newly assumed office and revolutionary party plotting grew daily more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Changsha, the new governor Yu Chengge had just taken office and revolutionary plotting grew more urgent by the day.

sentences.zh: 誠格慮新軍有異志，以中路巡防十營屬之，不就。

translations.literal: Chengge feared the new army harbored disloyal intent and placed the ten central-route patrol battalions under him; he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Chengge, fearing disloyalty in the new army, offered him the ten central-route patrol battalions; he refused.

sentences.zh: 誠格下席揖請至再，不獲已，始受事。

translations.literal: Chengge left his seat and bowed in invitation again and again; unable to refuse further, he at last accepted the charge.
translations.idiomatic: Chengge rose from his seat and bowed to him repeatedly; unable to refuse further, he at last accepted command.

sentences.zh: 甫三日，鄂亂起。

translations.literal: Only three days later turmoil broke out in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later rebellion broke out in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 九月朔，新軍變，將入城，協統蕭良臣遁，防軍為內應。

translations.literal: On the first day of the ninth month the new army mutinied and was about to enter the city. Assistant commander Xiao Liangchen fled, and the defense force served as inside collaborators.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the ninth month the new army mutinied and prepared to enter the city. Assistant commander Xiao Liangchen fled, and elements of the defense force acted as collaborators within.

sentences.zh: 忠浩方晨謁，隨誠格出，撫諭至再，勢洶洶不可遏，要誠格為都督。

translations.literal: Zhonghao was paying a morning call and followed Chengge out, soothing and instructing them again and again, but the momentum was furious and could not be checked; they demanded that Chengge become military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghao was on a morning call and went out with Chengge, reasoning with the mob again and again, but the crowd could not be restrained and demanded that Chengge become military governor.

sentences.zh: 誠格從間道出，召水師，水師亦變。

translations.literal: Chengge slipped out by a side route and summoned the naval force, but the naval force also mutinied.
translations.idiomatic: Chengge slipped out by a side route and called up the naval force, but the sailors mutinied as well.

sentences.zh: 誠格投江，左右援之，不得死。

translations.literal: Chengge threw himself into the river; those beside him pulled him out and he could not die.
translations.idiomatic: Chengge threw himself into the river, but his attendants pulled him out and he could not die.

sentences.zh: 忠浩猶留署，火起，護弁強之出，及門，遇亂兵，被執，脅降不從，劫之走，刃傷臂及股，至小吳門城樓，遂遇害。

translations.literal: Zhonghao still remained at the yamen. When fire broke out his bodyguards forced him out. At the gate he met disorderly troops, was seized, was pressed to surrender and would not, was dragged away, was cut on arm and thigh, and at the Xiaowumen gate tower was thereupon killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghao remained at headquarters. When fire broke out his guards forced him out. At the gate he was seized by rebel troops, refused to surrender, was dragged away with wounds to his arm and thigh, and was killed at the Xiaowumen gate tower.

sentences.zh: 家人奉喪歸葬，緣塗設奠者數百里。

translations.literal: His family bore the coffin home for burial; along the road offerings were set out for several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: His family bore his coffin home for burial, and mourners set out offerings along the route for several hundred li.

sentences.zh: 繼忠浩死者有楊讓梨。

translations.literal: Following Zhonghao in death was Yang Rangli.
translations.idiomatic: Among those who died after Zhonghao was Yang Rangli.

sentences.zh: 楊讓梨，字劭欽，籍湘鄉。

translations.literal: Yang Rangli, styled Shaoqin, was registered in Xiangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rangli, styled Shaoqin, was from Xiangxiang.

sentences.zh: 少與王珍子詩正友善。

translations.literal: In youth he was friendly with Wang Zhen's son Shizheng.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was close friends with Wang Zhen's son Shizheng.

sentences.zh: 詩正援台灣，戰失利，嘗負之以免，軍中咸壯之。

translations.literal: Shizheng went to aid Taiwan; when battle went badly he once carried Rangli on his back to save him, and all in the army admired the feat.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizheng went to aid Taiwan and the battle went badly, he once carried Rangli on his back to safety, and the whole army admired the deed.

sentences.zh: 積勳至守備。

translations.literal: He accumulated merit until he reached the rank of garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose on accumulated merit to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 轉戰新疆、河州、西寧，數有功，累擢參將，賜號鏗色巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He fought in turn in Xinjiang, Hezhou, and Xining, achieved merit repeatedly, was promoted in succession to brigade general, and was granted the title Kense Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in Xinjiang, Hezhou, and Xining, won repeated distinction, rose to brigade general, and was granted the title Kense Batulu.

sentences.zh: 既，還長沙，隸忠浩麾下。

translations.literal: Afterward he returned to Changsha and served under Zhonghao.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned to Changsha and served under Zhonghao.

sentences.zh: 宣統二年，補鎮筸鎮標中軍游擊。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuantong he was appointed central battalion mobile corps commander of the Zhenqian garrison standard.
translations.idiomatic: In 1910 he was appointed central battalion commander of the Zhenqian garrison.

sentences.zh: 明年，武漢事起，忠浩電調援長沙。

translations.literal: The next year trouble broke out at Wuhan; Zhonghao telegraphed to summon him to aid Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when rebellion broke out at Wuhan, Zhonghao telegraphed for him to reinforce Changsha.

sentences.zh: 次辰州，聞省城亂，乃扼辰龍關，誓死守。

translations.literal: Stopping at Chenzhou, he heard the provincial capital was in disorder and therefore held Chenlong Pass, swearing to defend to the death.
translations.idiomatic: At Chenzhou he heard the provincial capital had fallen into chaos and seized Chenlong Pass, swearing to hold it to the death.

sentences.zh: 筸兵故悍銳，為民軍所憚。

translations.literal: The Qian garrison troops were formerly fierce and sharp, and the revolutionary army feared them.
translations.idiomatic: The Qian garrison was famously fierce, and the revolutionary army feared them.

sentences.zh: 時總兵周瑞龍持兩端，其子瓚齎金至，將以餌筸兵，哨弁李鳳鳴潛告讓梨，得為備。

translations.literal: At the time Brigade General Zhou Ruilong wavered between two sides; his son Zan brought gold, intending to buy off the Qian troops. Sentinel officer Li Fengming secretly informed Rangli, and he was able to prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Brigade general Zhou Ruilong was wavering; his son Zan arrived with gold to bribe the Qian troops. Sentinel officer Li Fengming secretly warned Rangli, and he was able to prepare.

sentences.zh: 瑞龍稱疾，檄讓梨還，代以他將。

translations.literal: Ruilong claimed illness and ordered by dispatch that Rangli return, replacing him with another commander.
translations.idiomatic: Ruilong claimed illness, ordered Rangli back, and replaced him with another officer.

sentences.zh: 讓梨乃上書責以大義滅親，辭激昂，且傳檄捕瓚，瓚遁。

translations.literal: Rangli then submitted a letter rebuking him with the principle that righteousness overrides kinship, his words impassioned, and also issued a proclamation to arrest Zan; Zan fled.
translations.idiomatic: Rangli wrote a furious letter invoking the duty to put loyalty above family ties and issued a warrant for Zan's arrest; Zan fled.

sentences.zh: 已而瑞龍降，道府官委印綬去。

translations.literal: Before long Ruilong surrendered, and circuit and prefectural officials surrendered their seals and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ruilong surrendered, and circuit and prefectural officials abandoned their posts.

sentences.zh: 讓梨痛哭，犒遣軍士，獨棹小舟至清浪灘，踴身入水。

translations.literal: Rangli wept bitterly, rewarded and dismissed the soldiers, alone poled a small boat to Qinglang Beach, and leapt into the water.
translations.idiomatic: Rangli wept, rewarded and dismissed his soldiers, poled a small boat alone to Qinglang Beach, and threw himself into the water.

sentences.zh: 舟子泅出之，讓梨恚甚，曰：「奚活我為？」

translations.literal: The boatman swam out and pulled him up. Rangli was deeply angered and said, "Why keep me alive?"
translations.idiomatic: The boatman pulled him out. Rangli was furious and said, "Why did you save me?"

sentences.zh: 瓚出代其軍，遣人追縶讓梨及其子傳孔，鎖送長沙。

translations.literal: Zan came forth to replace his army, sent men to pursue and seize Rangli and his son Chuan Kong, and had them locked and sent to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Zan took command of the troops and sent men to seize Rangli and his son Chuan Kong, who were shackled and sent to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 迳常德，遇龍璋巡按西路，勸之不屈，遂斬之。

translations.literal: Passing through Changde he met Long Zhang on inspection tour of the western circuit, who urged him to yield; he would not bend, and was thereupon beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Changde he met Long Zhang, inspector of the western circuit, who urged him to submit; he refused and was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，肅衣冠北鄉拜，觀者萬餘人，皆泣下。

translations.literal: Facing execution he arranged cap and robes and bowed toward the north; more than ten thousand onlookers all wept.
translations.idiomatic: At the execution he dressed in his formal robes and bowed toward the north; more than ten thousand onlookers wept.

sentences.zh: 傳孔釋還。

translations.literal: Chuan Kong was released and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Chuan Kong was released and sent home.

sentences.zh: 有陳萁者，讓梨從子壻也。

translations.literal: There was one Chen Qi, Rangli's nephew by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Chen Qi, Rangli's nephew by marriage.

sentences.zh: 當讓梨被縛時，萁即奪起擊縛者，僕一人，攢刃交下，傷其首，斷一足，並死之。

translations.literal: When Rangli was bound, Qi at once sprang up and struck the binders. With one servant, blades rained down together, wounding his head and severing one foot, and both died.
translations.idiomatic: When Rangli was seized, Qi sprang up and attacked his captors. With a single servant he fought back until blades cut his head and severed a foot; both died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：辛亥之變，各省新軍既先發難，防營不能獨支，而京外旗兵久無軍備，又多被殘困，死行陣者，自寥寥可數。

translations.literal: The commentator says: In the change of 1911 the new armies of the provinces had already risen first; defense camps could not hold alone, while banner troops outside the capital had long lacked military preparation and were mostly trapped and slaughtered—those who died in battle were naturally few and countable.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: In the revolution of 1911 the provincial new armies struck first; defense garrisons could not hold alone. Banner troops outside the capital had long gone without proper arms and were often trapped and slaughtered, so those who died fighting were few.

sentences.zh: 志鈞等權輕勢孤，艱難搘柱，思以一隅挽全局；

translations.literal: Zhi Jun and others had light authority and stood alone, propping up the situation with difficulty, thinking to save the whole realm from one corner;
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Zhi Jun held little power and stood alone, struggling to shore up the situation and hoping to save the dynasty from a single corner of the empire;

sentences.zh: 及事不可為，乃以死報，志節皎然，可敬亦可哀矣！

translations.literal: when affairs could not be saved they repaid with death. Their resolve and integrity shine clear—worthy of respect and also deeply pitiable!
translations.idiomatic: when nothing more could be done they repaid the dynasty with their lives. Their integrity shines bright—admirable and deeply moving.
